Import user memory data from a `memcore.user_export.v1` JSON export. Set `dry_run=true` to validate without writes.
An exported fact id is kept only when this user already holds it (live or deleted); any other
fact is stored under an id derived from the organization, the user and the exported id, so restored ids can
differ from the export (see `docs/BACKUP_EXPORT.md`).

200.description: Import completed or dry-run validation summary

400.description: Validation error, nothing imported. Includes VALIDATION_ERROR with a message starting DUPLICATE_FACT_ID: two exported facts share one id, or would be stored under one id

session_id.description:
Optional client ID for the conversation session. Stored on every fact extracted from the
request. It also scopes `message_id`s: retries must send the same `session_id`. Omitting it
places the request's message IDs in the one session-less scope of the organization and user.
Empty or whitespace-only values and values over 200 characters are rejected with 400.

session_timestamp.description:
Optional time of the session: RFC 3339, or a date memcore can read (e.g. `2023-05-08`,
`8 May 2023`, `4:15 pm on 12 March, 2024`). Used for messages without their own `timestamp`.
An unreadable value is rejected with 400. With neither a session nor a message time, relative
dates ("last year") get no event time: the time memcore received the request is never used
as an anchor. Explicit dates ("March 2024") are kept either way.

oneOf.description:
Entity processing for this request (`MEMCORE_ENTITIES_ENABLED`); omitted when entities are
disabled, so responses are otherwise unchanged.

ApiKeyScopeResponse.description: API-facing scope labels (PascalCase) separate from core snake_case serde.

episodes_matched.description: Present only when episodes are enabled; episodes follow the fact retention window.

include_history.description:
Also use memories superseded by consolidation (`MEMCORE_CONSOLIDATION_MODE=llm_v2`), which
are otherwise left out. No effect in `legacy` mode. Default `false`.

event_time.description: A fact's source-supported event time; never set for an episode.

metadata.description: A fact's metadata (`null` for an episode).

observed_at.description: When the fact was stated or the message sent, as the client gave it. Not event time.

rank.description: 1-based position in the item's own search result list.

rerank_score.description:
The reranker's score, for candidates inside the rerank window when a reranker ran (the
score cache). Absent otherwise.

source_message_ids.description: A fact's source message IDs (empty for an episode).

vector_score.description: Raw vector similarity to the query; not normalised or rescaled.

CandidateSkipCountsResponse.description:
Why facts the model returned never became candidates.

These are losses inside extraction, before any memory decision. They used to be invisible:
a fact whose `memory_type` the parser did not recognise was dropped with no log, no metric and
no error, which is how memcore stored 634 memories from 5,882 conversation turns.

invalid_candidate.description: The fact failed validation — empty content, or a score outside 0.0..=1.0.

unknown_memory_type.description: The `memory_type` label was not in the vocabulary.

refresh_skipped.description: Background refreshes skipped at the per-process refresh budget.

scope.description: Metrics are aggregate counters for this API process only.

observed_at.description: When the memory was stated, as opposed to when it happened.

subject.description: Structured fields; omitted when the memory was stored without them.

raw_key.description: Raw API key returned only once at creation time.

EmbeddingDiagnosticsResponse.description:
The embedding provider's process-local diagnostics (a local model's queue depth,
queue wait and inference time); `diagnostics` is null for providers without any.

EntityAliasResponse.description: One name an entity goes by, and how it was added (a `merge` alias can be split back out).

EntityFactResponse.description: A fact linked to the entity (deleted facts are not listed).

mention.description: The name the fact used for the entity.

EntityProcessingSummaryResponse.description: What entity processing did for an add request (present only when entities are enabled).

rejected_mentions.description:
Mentions rejected because they are not grounded in the source messages or fact or
name no particular referent.

repaired_annotations.description: Annotations used after a deterministic syntax repair.

retried_annotations.description: Annotation requests that used their one retry after an unusable output.

is_speaker.description: A person named as a message speaker.

EpisodeSearchResultResponse.description: One episode: a stored source message (PII-redacted when redaction is on).

observed_at.description: The client's message or session time; never the time memcore received it.

score.description:
Vector similarity to the query (higher is better). Episode search is semantic only, so this
is the raw vector similarity, the same value as `vector_score`.

vector_score.description:
Raw vector similarity (cosine similarity with Qdrant), with the same meaning as
`vector_score` on memory search results; not normalised or rescaled.

EventTimeResponse.description:
When a fact happened: the span it covers and the message time it was resolved
against.

verified_reads.description: Identical full reads the export required (2).

ExportEntitiesResponse.description: The entity layer of a v3 export.

name_embedding.description:
Embedding of the canonical name, with the model and dimension that produced it.
Optional on import; an embedding from another model or dimension is never compared.

ExportEpisodeItemResponse.description:
An exported episode (source-message-level memory; content as stored, i.e. PII-redacted when
redaction was on).

subject.description:
Structured fields. Omitted when empty, so exports of facts written without
structured extraction are unchanged, and optional on import.

superseded_at.description:
When memcore marked the fact superseded; bookkeeping time, not a
real-world time. A superseded fact is no longer active. Omitted when unset; optional on
import.

superseded_by.description:
The fact that superseded this one, when it was stored (provenance only).
Omitted when unset; optional on import.

ExportTruncatedSectionResponse.description: One export section that stopped at its per-export limit.

limit.description: Exactly this many records of the section were exported.

FactDiscardCountsResponse.description:
Why extracted candidates were not stored.

`extracted` always equals
`added + updated + deleted + discarded.total + skipped.total`, so a rejected
memory is accounted for rather than silently dropped.

duplicate_content.description: Near-identical wording to an existing fact.

duplicate_embedding.description: Near-identical embedding to an existing fact.

invalid_classification.description: The classifier's output was invalid; the candidate was rejected, not stored.

no_op_decision.description: The classifier chose no-op, archive, or summarize instead of a write.

oneOf.description:
closure: ingestion recovery (omitted without an ingest journal). Informational:
it never makes the service unready; alert on `stalled`.

quality.description: The runtime quality tier and what it rests on.

imported_entities.description: Present only when the export carried entities (v3).

imported_episodes.description: Present only when the export carried episodes (v2).

manifest_consistent.description:
True only when the archive declares a complete export and matches its own
manifest. A consistency check, not proof of source completeness (the manifest is not
signed). Legacy and truncated archives are always false.

skipped_entities.description: Entities not imported because entities are disabled on this server.

skipped_episodes.description: Episodes not imported because episodes are disabled on this server.

state.description:
`idle`, `recovering` (normal backlog: in-flight requests, rollbacks within their window),
`stalled` (an operation older than three stale windows or claimed three times) or
`unavailable` (the journal could not be read).

MemoryContextItemResponse.description: One selected item, in context order.

message_id.description: An episode's client message id (absent for facts and for messages sent without one).

source_message_ids.description: The client message ids a fact was extracted from (absent when none were recorded).

tokens.description: cl100k_base tokens of this line alone (`token_count` counts the joined text).

MemoryContextRequest.description: `POST /api/v1/memories/context`: one user's server-side context, rendered by the server.

exclude_message_ids.description:
Client message ids whose **episodes** are left out of this context,
e.g. the `message_id`s of episodes already returned in another memory user's context for the
same answer prompt (a conversation stored for both participants keeps each message as an
episode of both, so concatenated contexts repeat them verbatim). Exact ids only; facts are
never removed; the packing rule continues over the remaining candidates. At most 2,000 ids of
at most 200 characters. Omitted or empty: the validated reference behaviour.

include_items.description: Also return the selected items with their scores, lines and per-line tokens.

packing.description:
`prefix` (the default unless the server sets `MEMCORE_CONTEXT_DEFAULT_PACKING`: the
rank-order prefix the reference was measured with, the first line that does not fit ends
the context), `fill` (opt-in: a line that does not fit is skipped and later lines are still
tried, in rank order, within the same budget) or `evidence` (opt-in: `fill` over a
fact-anchored order, see `d76_context::render_evidence`). Omitted: the server default.

token_budget.description: cl100k_base token budget for this user's context; default 1,500, 1–4,000.

budget_bound.description: True when the next candidate did not fit, i.e. the budget ended the context.

excluded_candidates.description: Episode candidates removed by `exclude_message_ids` (present only when ids were sent).

lines_skipped.description: With `fill` / `evidence`: the lines not kept (did not fit, or a redundant fact).

packing.description: `fill` or `evidence` when that packing was used (explicitly or as the server default); absent for `prefix`.

source.description: `e_merge` (facts and episodes) or `facts_only` (episodes disabled: (the facts-only form).

text.description: The selected lines joined with `\n`; `"<timestamp>: <text>"` per line.

MemoryEventOperationResponse.description: API-facing operation labels (PascalCase) separate from core snake_case serde.

message_id.description:
Optional client ID of this message occurrence, returned in a fact's `source_message_ids`.
Stable IDs are what make a retry safe: generate the ID once, when the message is created, and
send the same ID when retrying. An ID must be unique for its organization, `user_id` and
`session_id` across all requests, not only within one request; messages without a
`session_id` share one scope per organization and user. Two identical messages that were both
really sent need different IDs. Re-sending an ID with the same message (same role, `name`,
content and time) is a retry: the stored message is reused, not stored again. Reusing an ID
for a different message is rejected with 409 `MESSAGE_ID_CONFLICT`, and nothing from that
request is stored. Duplicate IDs within one request, empty or whitespace-only IDs and IDs over
200 characters are rejected with 400. Without IDs nothing is deduplicated. A request that
timed out may have been partly stored; `Retry-After` is only a timing hint. Concurrent
identical requests are not idempotent at the fact level: retry sequentially. IDs are checked
only when episode storage is on (`MEMCORE_EPISODES_ENABLED`, on in every shipped profile).

name.description: Optional display name of the speaker, so a fact can be attributed to a person.

timestamp.description:
Optional time the message was sent, in the same formats as `session_timestamp`. Relative
expressions in the message ("yesterday") are resolved against it (else against
`session_timestamp`; never against the receipt time). An unreadable value is rejected with
400.

event_time_unparsed.description:
Facts stored without an event time because `valid_at` could not be read. Counted in
`added`/`updated`, not in `skipped` — the fact survived, only its date did not.

extracted.description: Candidate facts extraction produced for this request.

invalid_source_message_ids.description: Source message IDs the model cited that were not in the request; dropped, never stored.

invalidated.description:
Stored memories superseded and kept as history (`MEMCORE_CONSOLIDATION_MODE=llm_v2`).
Omitted when zero, so `legacy` responses are unchanged.

noop.description:
Total candidates not stored. Equals `discarded.total`, and is kept under
the original `noop` name so existing clients keep working.

skipped.description: Facts the model returned that extraction could not use at all.

stored.description: Candidates that ended up stored (added + updated).

temporal_resolution.description:
How structured facts' event times were settled. All zero when structured
extraction is off.

MemoryTypeResponse.description: API-facing memory type labels (PascalCase) separate from core snake_case serde.

total_episodes.description: Episodes, counted separately from facts; present only when episodes are enabled.

source.description: `persistent` reads stored events; `memory` returns process-local aggregates only.

configured_tier.description: The tier the configuration alone would claim.

live_provider_verified.description: True only when a live chat probe passed in this process.

reference_mismatches.description: Reference-contract settings this configuration changes (names only).

validated_variants.description:
Validated variants of the frozen reference that this configuration enables, each with its own
validation record. A tier is never inherited silently: an enabled variant is listed here with
what was and was not shown equivalent. Empty when none is enabled.

bypassed.description: Provider without a known embedding identity (one uncached provider operation each).

followers.description: Waited for a concurrent flight (no provider operation).

hits.description: Served from a stored entry (no provider operation).

leaders.description: Started a single flight (one provider operation each).

provider_operations.description: Actual provider embedding operations started through the cache: leaders + bypassed.

requests.description: Query-embedding requests that reached the cache.

enabled.description: `false` when `MEMCORE_QUERY_EMBEDDING_CACHE_CAPACITY` is 0 (the default); counters are then 0.

scope.description: Metrics are aggregate counters for this API process only.

RetrievalModeRequest.description:
Which retrieval legs a search runs. Omitted means the server's `MEMCORE_SEARCH_STRATEGY`
(default `hybrid`, the fused search memcore has always run). `semantic` is vector only,
`fulltext` ranked full-text only, and `rrf` fuses the vector and full-text legs by Reciprocal
Rank Fusion over rank positions (`MEMCORE_RRF_K`).

SearchCandidatesRequest.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: one user's facts and episodes as one candidate list. Not a stable
retrieval contract.

episode_limit.description: Episode depth; default 100 (the reference depth), capped at `MEMCORE_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT`.

fact_limit.description: Semantic fact depth; default 100 (the reference depth), capped at `MEMCORE_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT`.

include_analysis.description: Return the query analysis (when query analysis is on).

reference_time.description:
RFC 3339 time that relative expressions in the query ("yesterday") are resolved against, when
query analysis is on. Never replaced by the server clock: without it they stay unresolved.

analysis.description: The query analysis, when requested and query analysis is on.

decomposition.description:
The decomposition attempt (provider, calls, accepted / rejected sub-queries, fallback), when
a decomposition provider is configured.

rerank_fallback.description: Why the reranker's order was not used, if it failed (the prior order is kept).

rerank_latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time of the reranker call, when a reranker is configured.

stages.description: The transformations applied, in order; empty in baseline mode.

SearchEpisodesRequest.description:
Semantic search over one user's episodes. No full-text leg, reranking or query
rewriting. `limit` follows the memory search rules (`MEMCORE_SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT`).

include_history.description:
Also return memories superseded by consolidation (`MEMCORE_CONSOLIDATION_MODE=llm_v2`) or by
a semantic related-fact matcher, which are otherwise left out; each such result carries a
`lifecycle` object. No effect in `legacy` mode. Default `false`.

oneOf.description: Retrieval legs to run; defaults to the server's `MEMCORE_SEARCH_STRATEGY`.

user_names.description:
Names the user `user_id` goes by (display name, aliases). Every memory in this user's scope
is from or about them, so these names are not used as full-text search terms; other names
in the query are. Ignored by the vector leg and by `hybrid`.

oneOf.description:
Present only on a result that is no longer current (returned with
`include_history`): a previous value, never the current one.

score.description: The engine's search-strategy score, which orders the results (unchanged).

vector_score.description:
Raw vector similarity from the semantic leg (cosine similarity with Qdrant), not normalised
or rescaled. Omitted when no vector leg returned this result (full-text mode, or a
keyword-only hybrid hit).

SearchResultLifecycleResponse.description: Why a search result is no longer current.

invalid_at.description: When it stopped being true in the real world, when known.

status.description: `superseded` (a later memory replaced it) or `invalidated` (it stopped being true).

superseded_at.description: When memcore marked it superseded (bookkeeping time, not an event time).

superseded_by.description: The memory that replaced it, when one was stored.

TemporalResolutionResponse.description: Per-outcome count of how structured facts' event times were settled.

deterministic_only.description: Only the resolver produced a time.

deterministic_override.description: They disagreed; the resolver's answer was used.

llm_only.description: Only the model produced a time (expression outside the resolver's patterns).

non_datable.description:
The time expression cannot be dated from the conversation ("recently", "every week", "when
I was 10", "for five years"); no event time is stored and the fact keeps its observation time.

rejected.description: The model's time was impossible and could not be replaced.

unanchored.description:
A relative expression ("last year", "yesterday") in a request with no client message or
session timestamp: nothing to resolve it against, so no event time is stored. memcore never
uses the time it received the request instead.

ungrounded.description:
The model gave a time with no expression behind it (usually the message's own date on a
timeless fact); ignored, and the fact keeps its observation time only.

oneOf.description:
Present only on a complete export (`complete=true`): exact section counts that an
import verifies before any write. Legacy and capped exports never carry it.
v3 exports only (entities enabled): entities, fact links and relations.

episodes.description: v2 exports only (episodes enabled). Absent from v1 exports, which are unchanged.

truncated.description:
Present only when the export is INCOMPLETE: each listed section reached its documented
per-export limit (facts 100, memory events 100, episodes 10,000) and later records were
not exported. Complete exports omit the field.

ValidatedVariant.description:
The validation record of a variant of the frozen reference.
`output-equivalent` means the stored state, contexts and answer prompts were shown identical to
the reference on the frozen replay; it does not mean operationally equivalent (provider calls,
usage, call budgets, circuit breaking and failure propagation differ by design).

context_parity.description: Context parity and the scope of its evidence.

equivalence.description: `output-equivalent`: stored state, contexts and prompts identical to the reference.

frozen_reference.description: The frozen reference it was validated against.

implementation.description: The implementation, with this build's version and source revision.

intentional_operational_differences.description: The operational behaviour that differs from the reference, by design.

operationally_equivalent.description: Always false for this variant: it changes provider traffic by design.

output_parity.description: Answer-output parity and the scope of its evidence.

prompt_parity.description: Prompt parity and the scope of its evidence.

stored_state_parity.description: Stored-state parity and the scope of its evidence.

reachable.description: Live reachability for network backends (Qdrant); `null` when nothing needs probing.

BearerAuth.description: Bearer API key. In dev mode use MEMCORE_DEV_API_KEY; in database mode use a stored key hash lookup.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Prometheus scrape endpoint (disabled by default; auth required by default)
